mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4% in the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 6% predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as higher labor market disengagement reduces corporate optimism and investment plans.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6% in the current month
regime_hint: High unemployment or weak wage growth
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of months when UNRATE > 6% (binomial test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real GDP) exceeds INDPRO by more than 10% in the prior quarter, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are expected to be positive as excess demand supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 / INDPRO > 1.10 in the prior quarter
regime_hint: Economic expansion with output gap expansion
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) when the output gap is expanding (GDPC1 > 1.10*INDPRO).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline of at least 3% in INDPRO for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as it signals contracting supply capacity and potential overvaluation.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive when INDPRO declines by ≥3% in two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive as low rates encourage equity investment.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive in 80% of months with FEDFUNDS < 1% for three months (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in PAYEMS (labor market activity) by over 20% in a month is associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return as it signals strong hiring and economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >20% in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises >20% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST (household spending) exceeds 105% of the prior month's value, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be positive reflecting strong consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses above 1.05 * previous month's value
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when HOUST > 1.05* prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of 5% or more indicates weak demand, predicting a negative S&P 5-day forward return as valuations may overcorrect.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by ≥5% in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive when RSAFS falls by ≥5% (p > 0.05).
